name: Music (AI-written, not yet reviewed)
description: 59 questions on music: artists, bands, instruments and songs by decade, from easy to hard (19 easy, 20 medium, 20 hard), written by Claude. Every question and answer needs checking by a person before anybody plays it.

source.name: Written by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) on 2026-10-05, from its own knowledge plus the pages each item cites: no API call. Each item's `source` names the page its fact was confirmed on, or "common knowledge" with a reason where the fact is universal. Fact-check pending: no item carries `checked` yet, so a separate fact-check pass still has to go through every item, and a person still reviews it by playing.

review.how: Check every question, answer and explanation. Fix or delete what is wrong, set status to 'reviewed' with your name and the date, then move the file to packs/ and list it in pack_library.js.

items.question: Which artist released the 1982 album Thriller?
items.explain: Thriller came out in November 1982 and became one of the best-selling albums ever.

items.question: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
items.explain: A standard guitar has six strings.

source.note: Universally known basic fact about the guitar.

items.question: Reggae music comes from which country?
items.explain: Reggae grew up in Kingston, Jamaica, made famous by Bob Marley and the Wailers.

items.question: Which band had the hit "Bohemian Rhapsody"?
items.explain: Queen released "Bohemian Rhapsody" in 1975 on A Night at the Opera.

items.question: Who was the Rolling Stones' lead singer when the band began in 1962?
items.explain: Mick Jagger fronted the Rolling Stones from the very start.

items.question: Which instrument did Jimi Hendrix famously play?
items.explain: Jimi Hendrix is remembered as one of the greatest electric guitarists.

source.note: Hendrix as a guitarist is universally known.

items.question: Which country singer had a hit with "Jolene"?
items.explain: "Jolene" is one of Dolly Parton's best-loved songs.

source.note: Dolly Parton's signature song; widely known.

items.question: Who sang the famous love theme from the 1997 movie Titanic?
items.explain: Celine Dion sang the movie's love theme, and it became a worldwide hit.

source.note: Widely known film song and singer.

items.question: What is the stick a conductor waves called?
items.explain: Conductors use a short stick called a baton so the players can follow the beat.

items.question: How many musicians play in a trio?
items.explain: A trio is a group of three.

items.question: The trumpet, trombone and tuba belong to which family of instruments?
items.explain: Trumpets, trombones, tubas and French horns make up the brass section.

items.question: Which city is nicknamed "Music City" and is famous for country music?
items.explain: Nashville, Tennessee is home of the Grand Ole Opry and known as Music City.

items.question: What was Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart famous for?
items.explain: Mozart was one of the greatest composers of classical music.

source.note: Mozart as a composer is universally known.

items.question: Which instrument is Elton John famous for playing?
items.explain: Elton John sings while playing the piano.

source.note: Elton John as a pianist is widely known.

items.question: Which singer had a big 2013 hit with the song "Happy"?
items.explain: Pharrell Williams released "Happy" in 2013, and it was everywhere in 2014.

items.question: Which ballet features the Sugar Plum Fairy?
items.explain: Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker includes the Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy.

items.question: Which band was John Lennon a member of?
items.explain: John Lennon was a founding member of the Beatles.

source.note: Universally known fact about the Beatles.

items.question: Which instrument is played with a bow and held under the chin?
items.explain: The violin rests under the chin and is played with a bow.

items.question: Who sang "Purple Rain"?
items.explain: Prince released Purple Rain in 1984, with a movie of the same name.

items.question: In which year was the Woodstock music festival held?
items.explain: Woodstock took place on a dairy farm in Bethel, New York, in August 1969.

items.question: Which band released the 1991 album Nevermind?
items.explain: Nirvana's Nevermind brought the Seattle grunge sound to the whole world.

items.question: Motown Records was founded in which city?
items.explain: Motown began in Detroit in 1959; its name blends "motor" and "town."

items.question: Who was the lead singer of the Supremes?
items.explain: Diana Ross led the Supremes, Motown's most successful girl group.

items.question: Who composed The Four Seasons?
items.explain: Vivaldi's Four Seasons is a set of four violin concertos, one for each season.

items.question: Who composed "Rhapsody in Blue"?
items.explain: Gershwin premiered Rhapsody in Blue in New York in 1924, playing the piano himself.

items.question: Which Beethoven symphony includes the "Ode to Joy"?
items.explain: The "Ode to Joy" comes in Beethoven's Ninth, his last symphony, from 1824.

items.question: How many keys does a standard modern piano have?
items.explain: A standard piano has 88 keys: 52 white and 36 black.

items.question: A string quartet is two violins, a viola, and which other instrument?
items.explain: The classic string quartet is two violins, a viola and a cello.

items.question: Which band released The Dark Side of the Moon in 1973?
items.explain: Pink Floyd's album is famous for its prism-and-rainbow cover.

items.question: Which band released the 1977 album Rumours?
items.explain: Fleetwood Mac's Rumours won the Grammy for Album of the Year.

items.question: Which group wrote and sang the big hits on the Saturday Night Fever soundtrack?
items.explain: The Bee Gees gave the film "Stayin' Alive" and "Night Fever."

items.question: Whose 1954 recording became a huge hit after it opened the 1955 film Blackboard Jungle?
items.explain: Bill Haley and His Comets' song took off after it opened Blackboard Jungle.

items.question: Who released the 1975 album Born to Run?
items.explain: Born to Run was Bruce Springsteen's breakthrough, made with the E Street Band.

items.question: Which country star wrote the ballad that Whitney Houston turned into a giant hit for The Bodyguard (1992)?
items.explain: Dolly Parton wrote and first recorded the song in 1973.

items.question: The rock band U2 comes from which city?
items.explain: U2 is an Irish band from Dublin.

items.question: In 2012, which song's video became the first on YouTube to reach one billion views?
items.explain: Psy's "Gangnam Style" from South Korea passed one billion views in December 2012.

items.question: Taylor Swift's first album, in 2006, was mainly which style of music?
items.explain: Taylor Swift started out in country music; her first single was "Tim McGraw."

items.question: Jimmy Page, Robert Plant, John Paul Jones and John Bonham made up which band?
items.explain: Led Zeppelin formed in London in 1968.

items.question: Mark Ronson's 2014 hit "Uptown Funk" featured which singer?
items.explain: "Uptown Funk" by Mark Ronson featuring Bruno Mars spent 14 weeks at No. 1.

items.question: Which architect designed the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame building in Cleveland?
items.explain: I. M. Pei designed the museum, which opened in 1995.

items.question: The Moondog Coronation Ball in Cleveland, often called the first major rock and roll concert, took place in which year?
items.explain: Alan Freed's Moondog Coronation Ball was held at the Cleveland Arena on March 21, 1952.

items.question: Who founded Motown Records?
items.explain: Berry Gordy Jr. started the label in Detroit in 1959.

items.question: Ahmet Ertegun, who helped found the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1983, founded which record label?
items.explain: Ertegun was the founder and chairman of Atlantic Records.

items.question: Which instrument usually plays the note an orchestra tunes to?
items.explain: By a 300-year-old custom, the oboe gives the orchestra its tuning note.

items.question: Which instrument plays the famous high solo at the very start of Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring?
items.explain: A bassoon opens the piece, played so high it is hard to recognize.

items.question: Which instrument plays the famous swooping opening of Rhapsody in Blue?
items.explain: A clarinet glissando opens the piece, an effect Gershwin kept after hearing it in rehearsal.

items.question: Who composed "Take Five," the Dave Brubeck Quartet's 1959 jazz hit?
items.explain: Saxophonist Paul Desmond wrote "Take Five" in unusual 5/4 time.

items.question: Which jazz trumpeter released the 1959 album Kind of Blue?
items.explain: Kind of Blue, with John Coltrane and Bill Evans, is often called Miles Davis's masterpiece.

items.question: When MTV launched in 1981, the first music video it played was by which band?
items.explain: MTV opened on August 1, 1981 with a video by the Buggles.

items.question: In Ravel's Bolero, which instrument plays the same rhythm from start to finish?
items.explain: A snare drum repeats the same rhythm 169 times while the music slowly grows louder.

items.question: How many Brandenburg Concertos did Johann Sebastian Bach write?
items.explain: Bach presented the six Brandenburg Concertos in 1721.

items.question: Which composer is often called the "father of the string quartet"?
items.explain: Haydn shaped the string quartet into four roughly equal partners.

items.question: Who is credited with inventing the piano, around the year 1700?
items.explain: Bartolomeo Cristofori of Padua, Italy, built the first pianos.

items.question: Which famous artist was credited as producer of the 1967 album The Velvet Underground & Nico?
items.explain: Andy Warhol was the credited producer and also designed the banana cover.

items.question: The band R.E.M. formed in 1980 in which college town?
items.explain: R.E.M. began with four University of Georgia students in Athens.

items.question: Who directed Stop Making Sense, the 1984 Talking Heads concert film?
items.explain: Jonathan Demme's film is sometimes called the greatest concert film ever made.

items.question: Paul Simon's 1986 album Graceland drew heavily on the music of which country?
items.explain: Simon recorded with South African musicians, including Ladysmith Black Mambazo.

items.question: At which event did Bob Dylan famously play with electric instruments in 1965?
items.explain: Dylan going electric at Newport in July 1965 upset many folk fans.

items.question: The "Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy" in The Nutcracker features which bell-like keyboard instrument?
items.explain: Tchaikovsky used the celesta for its shimmering, bell-like sound.
